R/coherence.R
content:
# Global coherence in escalation, as an escalation selector decorator.
#
# Do not recommend a dose above the current (last given) dose while the
# observed DLT rate at the current dose exceeds the target. Mirrors
# `global_coherent_esc` in dtpcrm::applied_titecrm(), which the legacy app
# used. Written to slot into an escalation/dtptite design chain, e.g.
#
#   get_dfcrm_tite(skeleton, target) |>
#     enforce_global_coherence() |>
#     apply_dtp(t_max, obswin)

#' Enforce global coherence in escalation
#'
#' @param parent_selector_factory A `selector_factory` object.
#' @param target DLT rate the observed rate is compared with. When `NULL`
#'   (default), the parent's `tox_target()` is used at fit time.
#' @return A `coherent_selector_factory` object.
enforce_global_coherence <- function(parent_selector_factory, target = NULL) {
  if (!is.null(target)) {
    stopifnot(is.numeric(target), length(target) == 1, target > 0, target < 1)
  }
  x <- list(parent = parent_selector_factory, target = target)
  class(x) <- c("coherent_selector_factory",
                "derived_dose_selector_factory",
                "selector_factory")
  x
}

fit.coherent_selector_factory <- function(selector_factory, outcomes, ...) {
  parent_selector <- selector_factory$parent |> escalation::fit(outcomes, ...)
  target <- selector_factory$target
  if (is.null(target)) target <- escalation::tox_target(parent_selector)
  x <- list(parent = parent_selector, target = target)
  class(x) <- c("coherent_selector", "derived_dose_selector", "selector")
  x
}

recommended_dose.coherent_selector <- function(x, ...) {
  rec <- escalation::recommended_dose(x$parent, ...)
  doses <- escalation::doses_given(x)
  if (is.na(rec) || length(doses) == 0) return(rec)

  current <- utils::tail(doses, 1)
  at_current <- doses == current
  observed_rate <- sum(escalation::tox(x)[at_current]) / sum(at_current)
  if (observed_rate > x$target && rec > current) {
    return(as.integer(current))
  }
  rec
}

# The app sources this file rather than installing it as a package, so
# register the methods with escalation's generics explicitly; dispatch from
# inside escalation and dtptite (e.g. DTP projection refits) then finds them.
registerS3method("fit", "coherent_selector_factory",
                 fit.coherent_selector_factory,
                 envir = asNamespace("escalation"))
registerS3method("recommended_dose", "coherent_selector",
                 recommended_dose.coherent_selector,
                 envir = asNamespace("escalation"))

name: R/design.R
content:
# DTP-TITE-CRM design: the escalation/dtptite chain built from app settings.

#' Calibrate a TITE-CRM skeleton
#'
#' Wraps [dfcrm::getprior()] with the empiric working model, the model the
#' design always fits (the legacy app calibrated with the logistic model
#' but fitted the empiric one).
#'
#' @param target Target DLT rate.
#' @param halfwidth Half-width of the indifference interval.
#' @param prior_mtd Prior guess of the MTD (dose level).
#' @param num_doses Number of dose levels.
#' @return Numeric vector of prior DLT probabilities, one per dose.
calibrate_skeleton <- function(target, halfwidth, prior_mtd, num_doses) {
  stopifnot(prior_mtd >= 1, prior_mtd <= num_doses, halfwidth > 0)
  if (target - halfwidth <= 0 || target + halfwidth >= 1) {
    stop("The indifference interval target +/- halfwidth must lie within ",
         "(0, 1).", call. = FALSE)
  }
  # getprior() warns "NaNs produced" on bad inputs; the check below gives
  # a clearer error instead.
  skeleton <- suppressWarnings(
    dfcrm::getprior(halfwidth = halfwidth, target = target, nu = prior_mtd,
                    nlevel = num_doses, model = "empiric")
  )
  if (anyNA(skeleton) || any(skeleton <= 0 | skeleton >= 1) ||
      is.unsorted(skeleton, strictly = TRUE)) {
    stop("Calibration did not give increasing DLT probabilities within ",
         "(0, 1); try a smaller halfwidth.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  skeleton
}

#' Prior probability that each dose is the MTD
#'
#' Under the empiric model with `beta ~ N(0, variance)`, dose `i` is the
#' model's MTD when `beta` falls in its indifference interval, as given by
#' [dfcrm::crmsens()]. The outer intervals are unbounded.
#'
#' @param skeleton Prior DLT probabilities, one per dose.
#' @param target Target DLT rate.
#' @param variance Prior variance of the model parameter.
#' @return Numeric vector of probabilities, one per dose, summing to 1.
prior_mtd_distribution <- function(skeleton, target, variance) {
  stopifnot(variance > 0)
  hset <- dfcrm::crmsens(skeleton, target = target, model = "empiric",
                         detail = TRUE)$Hset
  cuts <- hset[-nrow(hset), 2]
  diff(c(0, stats::pnorm(cuts, mean = 0, sd = sqrt(variance)), 1))
}

#' Least informative prior variance (Lee and Cheung, 2011)
#'
#' The variance whose prior MTD distribution ([prior_mtd_distribution()])
#' is closest to uniform, by Kullback-Leibler divergence. The search over
#' the prior standard deviation is continuous: a coarse grid, then
#' [stats::optimize()] around its best point.
#'
#' @param skeleton Prior DLT probabilities, one per dose.
#' @param target Target DLT rate.
#' @param sd_min,sd_max Range of prior standard deviations searched; a
#'   warning is given when the optimum is at either limit, as then the
#'   least informative variance lies outside the range.
#' @return The prior variance.
#' @references Lee SM, Cheung YK (2011). Calibration of prior variance in
#'   the Bayesian continual reassessment method. Statistics in Medicine
#'   30(17):2081-2089.
least_informative_variance <- function(skeleton, target, sd_min = 0.001,
                                       sd_max = 10) {
  stopifnot(is.numeric(sd_min), is.numeric(sd_max), length(sd_min) == 1,
            length(sd_max) == 1, sd_min > 0, sd_max > sd_min)
  k <- length(skeleton)
  divergence <- function(sd) {
    mu <- prior_mtd_distribution(skeleton, target, sd^2)
    sum(ifelse(mu > 0, mu * log(mu * k), 0))
  }
  # A coarse grid first, so optimize() starts in the right basin.
  grid <- exp(seq(log(sd_min), log(sd_max), length.out = 250))
  best <- which.min(vapply(grid, divergence, numeric(1)))
  lower <- grid[max(best - 1, 1)]
  upper <- grid[min(best + 1, length(grid))]
  sd <- stats::optimize(divergence, c(lower, upper), tol = 1e-10)$minimum
  # Judge the refined optimum, not the grid point: it is at a limit only
  # if optimize() ran into it.
  at_limit <- function(limit) abs(log(sd / limit)) < 1e-4
  if (at_limit(sd_min) || at_limit(sd_max)) {
    warning(sprintf(
      "The least informative prior SD is at the search limit (%g); it lies outside [%g, %g].",
      if (at_limit(sd_min)) sd_min else sd_max, sd_min, sd_max
    ), call. = FALSE)
  }
  sd^2
}

#' Beta prior parameters from a prior mean and effective sample size
#'
#' @param mean Prior mean DLT rate.
#' @param ess Prior effective sample size.
#' @return A list with `a` and `b`.
beta_prior_from_mean <- function(mean, ess) {
  stopifnot(mean > 0, mean < 1, ess > 0)
  list(a = mean * ess, b = (1 - mean) * ess)
}

#' Build the DTP-TITE-CRM design
#'
#' The chain is, in order: TITE-CRM (empiric model), safety stopping at the
#' lowest dose, dose-skipping restrictions, global coherence, then DTP. This
#' follows the order used in dtptite's own tests
#' (tests/testthat/test-depth-valve.R).
#'
#' @param skeleton Prior DLT probabilities, one per dose.
#' @param target Target DLT rate.
#' @param obswin DLT observation window, in days.
#' @param variance Prior variance of the model parameter.
#' @param no_skip_esc,no_skip_deesc Forbid skipping doses when escalating or
#'   de-escalating ([escalation::dont_skip_doses()]: at most one level from
#'   the last dose given).
#' @param global_coherence Apply [enforce_global_coherence()].
#' @param stop_confidence Confidence level for stopping for toxicity at the
#'   lowest dose, or `NULL` for no stopping rule.
#' @param stop_n_min Patients needed at the lowest dose before the stopping
#'   rule applies.
#' @param stop_a,stop_b Beta prior for the stopping rule. Defaults to the
#'   weakly informative Be(target, 1 - target): mean at the target, effective
#'   sample size 1.
#' @param t_max Longest wait DTP considers, in days. Defaults to `obswin`.
#' @return A list with `parent` (the design without DTP, refitted for each
#'   projected day) and `dtp` (the full design).
build_design <- function(skeleton, target, obswin, variance = 1.34,
                         no_skip_esc = TRUE, no_skip_deesc = TRUE,
                         global_coherence = TRUE,
                         stop_confidence = NULL, stop_n_min = 1,
                         stop_a = target, stop_b = 1 - target,
                         t_max = obswin) {
  stopifnot(all(skeleton > 0), all(skeleton < 1), !is.unsorted(skeleton),
            variance > 0)

  parent <- escalation::get_dfcrm_tite(skeleton = skeleton, target = target,
                                       model = "empiric",
                                       scale = sqrt(variance))
  if (!is.null(stop_confidence)) {
    parent <- parent |>
      dtptite::stop_for_beta_binomial_toxicity(
        dose = 1, tox_threshold = target, confidence = stop_confidence,
        a = stop_a, b = stop_b, n_min = stop_n_min
      )
  }
  if (no_skip_esc || no_skip_deesc) {
    parent <- parent |>
      escalation::dont_skip_doses(when_escalating = no_skip_esc,
                                  when_deescalating = no_skip_deesc)
  }
  if (global_coherence) {
    parent <- parent |> enforce_global_coherence()
  }

  list(
    parent = parent,
    dtp = parent |> dtptite::apply_dtp(t_max = t_max, obswin = obswin,
                                       verbose = FALSE)
  )
}

name: R/dtp_pathway.R
content:
# Dose Transition Pathway over calendar days.
#
# dtptite::apply_dtp() answers "how long until the recommendation rises?".
# The app also needs the whole pathway: for each future day, assuming no
# new DLTs, would the model de-escalate (D), stay (S) or escalate (E)
# relative to the current dose, or stop? Unlike apply_dtp(), only patients
# still being followed for DLT accrue follow-up; withdrawn patients keep
# their partial weight.

#' Project the dose recommendation day by day
#'
#' @param design The design *without* DTP, e.g. `build_design()$parent`.
#' @param data Patients in entry order, with columns `dose`, `tox`,
#'   `weight` and `monitored` (logical: still followed for DLT). The last
#'   row's dose is the current dose.
#' @param day_of_assessment Study day of the analysis (T_A).
#' @param obswin DLT observation window, in days.
#' @param t_max Longest wait to project, in days (`>= 0`, `Inf` allowed).
#'   Defaults to the time until every monitored patient completes
#'   follow-up.
#' @return A list of class `dtp_pathway` with:
#'   \describe{
#'     \item{days}{One row per projected day: `day`, `wait` (days after
#'       T_A), `dose` (recommended, `NA` if stopped), `decision` (`"D"`,
#'       `"S"`, `"E"` or `"Stop"`).}
#'     \item{runs}{Consecutive days with the same dose and decision:
#'       `from_day`, `to_day`, `dose`, `decision`.}
#'     \item{current_dose, recommended_dose}{Last dose given; recommendation
#'       at T_A.}
#'     \item{complete_day}{Day every monitored patient completes follow-up
#'       (T_A when none is pending), even when `t_max` stops `days` earlier.}
#'     \item{fits}{Fitted selectors: `current` (T_A), `complete` (all
#'       monitored patients fully followed up, even when `t_max` stops the
#'       projected days earlier) and `changes` (one per run, at its first
#'       day).}
#'   }
dtp_pathway <- function(design, data, day_of_assessment, obswin,
                        t_max = NULL) {
  stopifnot(nrow(data) > 0,
            all(c("dose", "tox", "weight", "monitored") %in% names(data)))
  # Same checks as dtptite::apply_dtp().
  stopifnot(is.numeric(obswin), length(obswin) == 1, is.finite(obswin),
            obswin > 0)
  if (!is.null(t_max)) {
    stopifnot(is.numeric(t_max), length(t_max) == 1, !is.na(t_max),
              t_max >= 0)
  }
  outcomes <- data.frame(dose = data$dose, tox = data$tox,
                         weight = data$weight, cohort = seq_len(nrow(data)))
  current_dose <- utils::tail(data$dose, 1)

  pending <- data$monitored & data$tox == 0 & data$weight < 1
  # Days until every monitored patient completes follow-up; t_max may cap
  # the projected days, but not the complete-follow-up fit.
  complete_wait <- if (any(pending)) {
    # Rounding first stops float error adding a day, e.g. (1 - 10/30) * 30
    # is 20.000000000000004.
    ceiling(round(max(1 - data$weight[pending]) * obswin, 8))
  } else {
    0
  }
  horizon <- if (is.null(t_max)) complete_wait else min(complete_wait, t_max)

  fit_at <- function(wait) {
    projected <- outcomes
    projected$weight[pending] <- pmin(
      1, data$weight[pending] + wait / obswin
    )
    escalation::fit(design, projected)
  }

  waits <- seq(0, horizon)
  fits <- lapply(waits, fit_at)
  doses <- vapply(fits, function(f) {
    rec <- escalation::recommended_dose(f)
    if (is.na(rec)) NA_integer_ else as.integer(rec)
  }, integer(1))
  decision <- ifelse(is.na(doses), "Stop",
                     ifelse(doses > current_dose, "E",
                            ifelse(doses < current_dose, "D", "S")))

  days <- data.frame(day = day_of_assessment + waits, wait = waits,
                     dose = doses, decision = decision)

  key <- paste(days$decision, days$dose)
  starts <- which(c(TRUE, key[-1] != key[-length(key)]))
  ends <- c(starts[-1] - 1, length(key))
  runs <- data.frame(from_day = days$day[starts], to_day = days$day[ends],
                     dose = days$dose[starts],
                     decision = days$decision[starts])

  structure(
    list(
      days = days,
      runs = runs,
      current_dose = current_dose,
      recommended_dose = doses[1],
      day_of_assessment = day_of_assessment,
      complete_day = day_of_assessment + complete_wait,
      fits = list(current = fits[[1]],
                  complete = if (horizon < complete_wait) {
                    fit_at(complete_wait)
                  } else {
                    fits[[length(fits)]]
                  },
                  changes = fits[starts])
    ),
    class = "dtp_pathway"
  )
}

#' First day the pathway reaches a decision
#'
#' @param pathway A `dtp_pathway`.
#' @param decision One of `"E"`, `"S"`, `"D"`, `"Stop"`.
#' @return The study day, or `NA` if the decision is never reached.
first_day_of <- function(pathway, decision) {
  hit <- pathway$runs$from_day[pathway$runs$decision == decision]
  if (length(hit)) hit[1] else NA_real_
}

print.dtp_pathway <- function(x, ...) {
  cat(sprintf("DTP from day %d, current dose %d\n", x$day_of_assessment,
              x$current_dose))
  print(x$runs, row.names = FALSE)
  invisible(x)
}

name: R/grid.R
content:
# The editable patient grid: trial data <-> rhandsontable frame.
#
# The grid shows patients sorted by entry day (P1, P2, ... as in the plots)
# with derived columns: days followed for Ongoing and Completed patients
# (read-only) and the TITE weight (blank for non-evaluable patients, who
# are not in the model).

grid_columns <- c("Dose", "Entry day", "Status", "Days followed",
                  "Evaluable", "Weight")

#' Canonical trial data: typed columns, sorted by entry day
#'
#' Days followed are kept only where they are entered (DLT, Withdrawn).
#'
#' @param trial A data.frame with `dose`, `entry_day`, `status` and
#'   optionally `days_followed` and `evaluable` (all evaluable when
#'   missing).
#' @return The same patients with numeric `dose`, `entry_day`,
#'   `days_followed`, character `status` and logical `evaluable`, sorted by
#'   entry day (missing last, ties in input order).
canonical_trial <- function(trial) {
  days <- if (is.null(trial$days_followed)) NA_real_ else
    suppressWarnings(as.numeric(trial$days_followed))
  out <- data.frame(
    dose = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(trial$dose))),
    entry_day = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(trial$entry_day)),
    status = as.character(trial$status),
    days_followed = days,
    evaluable = if (is.null(trial$evaluable)) rep(TRUE, nrow(trial)) else
      parse_evaluable(trial$evaluable)
  )
  out$days_followed[!out$status %in% c("DLT", "Withdrawn")] <- NA_real_
  out <- out[order(out$entry_day, na.last = TRUE), , drop = FALSE]
  rownames(out) <- NULL
  out
}

#' Grid frame shown to the user
#'
#' @param trial Canonical trial data, see [canonical_trial()].
#' @inheritParams normalise_trial_data
#' @return A data.frame with [grid_columns]; days followed are derived for
#'   Ongoing and Completed patients, and the weight is `NA` when the row is
#'   incomplete or out of range, or the patient is not evaluable.
grid_frame <- function(trial, day_of_assessment, obswin) {
  derived <- tryCatch(
    normalise_trial_data(trial, day_of_assessment, obswin),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  days <- trial$days_followed
  weight <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(trial))
  if (!is.null(derived) && nrow(derived) == nrow(trial)) {
    days <- derived$days_followed
    ok <- !is.na(derived$weight) & derived$weight >= 0 &
      derived$weight <= 1 & derived$evaluable %in% TRUE
    weight[ok] <- derived$weight[ok]
  }
  out <- data.frame(
    as.character(trial$dose), trial$entry_day, trial$status, days,
    trial$evaluable, weight
  )
  names(out) <- grid_columns
  out
}

#' Trial data from the edited grid
#'
#' @param grid A data.frame with [grid_columns], as from
#'   [rhandsontable::hot_to_r()].
#' @return Canonical trial data. A patient switched to DLT or Withdrawn
#'   keeps the days followed the grid showed for them.
trial_from_grid <- function(grid) {
  canonical_trial(data.frame(
    dose = grid[["Dose"]],
    entry_day = grid[["Entry day"]],
    status = grid[["Status"]],
    days_followed = grid[["Days followed"]],
    evaluable = grid[["Evaluable"]]
  ))
}

#' A new grid row: next patient at the last dose, entering on T_A
#'
#' @param trial Canonical trial data.
#' @inheritParams normalise_trial_data
add_patient <- function(trial, day_of_assessment) {
  last_dose <- utils::tail(trial$dose[!is.na(trial$dose)], 1)
  canonical_trial(rbind(trial, data.frame(
    dose = if (length(last_dose)) last_dose else 1,
    entry_day = day_of_assessment, status = "Ongoing",
    days_followed = NA_real_, evaluable = TRUE
  )))
}

#' Editable rhandsontable for the grid
#'
#' @param frame A [grid_frame()].
#' @param num_doses Number of dose levels (dropdown choices).
render_grid <- function(frame, num_doses) {
  derived_rows <- which(frame$Status %in% c("Ongoing", "Completed"))
  hot <- rhandsontable::rhandsontable(
    frame, rowHeaders = paste0("P", seq_len(nrow(frame))),
    # Natural height; long trials scroll inside the grid.
    stretchH = "all", height = if (nrow(frame) > 15) 420
  ) |>
    rhandsontable::hot_col("Dose", type = "dropdown",
                           source = as.character(seq_len(num_doses)),
                           strict = TRUE) |>
    rhandsontable::hot_col("Status", type = "dropdown",
                           source = trial_statuses, strict = TRUE) |>
    rhandsontable::hot_col(c("Entry day", "Days followed"), format = "0") |>
    rhandsontable::hot_col("Evaluable", type = "checkbox") |>
    rhandsontable::hot_col("Weight", readOnly = TRUE, format = "0.00") |>
    rhandsontable::hot_cols(renderer = "
      function (instance, td, row, col, prop, value, cellProperties) {
        Handsontable.renderers.getRenderer(cellProperties.type || 'text')
          .apply(this, arguments);
        if (cellProperties.readOnly) {
          td.style.background = '#F8F9FA';
          td.style.color = '#616466';
        }
      }") |>
    rhandsontable::hot_context_menu(allowRowEdit = TRUE,
                                    allowColEdit = FALSE)
  for (row in derived_rows) {
    hot <- rhandsontable::hot_cell(hot, row, "Days followed",
                                   readOnly = TRUE)
  }
  hot
}

name: R/inputs.R
content:
# Trial data input: from what sites record (days) to what dtptite needs
# (TITE weights).
#
# Each patient has a dose level, an entry day and a DLT-follow-up status:
#   Ongoing    still being followed for DLT; days followed are derived from
#              the day of assessment and projected forward by DTP
#   Completed  completed the DLT observation window without a DLT
#   DLT        had a DLT (weight 1, as in dfcrm and escalation)
#   Withdrawn  left DLT follow-up early without a DLT (e.g. progression);
#              their partial weight is frozen
#
# Each patient is also evaluable for DLT or not (e.g. replaced); only
# evaluable patients go into the model and the dose transition pathway.

trial_statuses <- c("Ongoing", "Completed", "DLT", "Withdrawn")

#' Read evaluability from logical, Yes/No or 1/0 values
#'
#' @param x A vector of evaluability values.
#' @return A logical vector, `NA` where a value is missing or not
#'   recognised (reported by [validate_trial_data()]).
parse_evaluable <- function(x) {
  if (is.logical(x)) return(x)
  key <- tolower(trimws(as.character(x)))
  out <- rep(NA, length(key))
  out[key %in% c("true", "yes", "y", "1")] <- TRUE
  out[key %in% c("false", "no", "n", "0")] <- FALSE
  out
}

#' Normalise trial data and derive TITE weights
#'
#' @param data A data.frame with columns `dose`, `entry_day`, `status`,
#'   `days_followed` and optionally `evaluable` (all evaluable when
#'   missing). `days_followed` is only used for DLT and Withdrawn patients;
#'   it may be `NA` otherwise.
#' @param day_of_assessment Study day of the analysis (T_A).
#' @param obswin Length of the DLT observation window, in days.
#' @return `data` sorted by entry day with `patient`, `evaluable`, `tox`,
#'   `monitored`, `days_followed` (derived where needed) and `weight`
#'   columns added. Non-evaluable patients are kept; see
#'   [evaluable_patients()].
normalise_trial_data <- function(data, day_of_assessment, obswin) {
  stopifnot(is.data.frame(data),
            all(c("dose", "entry_day", "status") %in% names(data)))
  if (!"days_followed" %in% names(data)) {
    data$days_followed <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(data))
  }
  if (!"evaluable" %in% names(data)) {
    data$evaluable <- rep(TRUE, nrow(data))
  }

  data <- data[order(data$entry_day), , drop = FALSE]
  rownames(data) <- NULL
  status <- as.character(data$status)
  days <- as.numeric(data$days_followed)

  days[status == "Ongoing"] <- pmin(
    day_of_assessment - data$entry_day[status == "Ongoing"] + 1, obswin
  )
  days[status == "Completed"] <- obswin

  data.frame(
    patient = seq_len(nrow(data)),
    dose = as.integer(data$dose),
    entry_day = as.numeric(data$entry_day),
    status = factor(status, levels = trial_statuses),
    evaluable = parse_evaluable(data$evaluable),
    days_followed = days,
    tox = as.integer(status == "DLT"),
    monitored = status == "Ongoing",
    weight = ifelse(status == "DLT", 1, pmin(days / obswin, 1))
  )
}

#' Patients that go into the model
#'
#' @param data Output of [normalise_trial_data()].
#' @return The evaluable patients, in entry order and keeping their patient
#'   numbers; the last row's dose is the current dose.
evaluable_patients <- function(data) {
  data[data$evaluable %in% TRUE, , drop = FALSE]
}

#' Convert normalised trial data to escalation/dtptite outcomes
#'
#' @param data Output of [normalise_trial_data()].
#' @return A data.frame with columns `dose`, `tox`, `weight`, `cohort`, in
#'   entry order (escalation takes the last row as the current dose).
to_outcomes <- function(data) {
  data.frame(dose = data$dose, tox = data$tox, weight = data$weight,
             cohort = seq_len(nrow(data)))
}

#' Validate trial data before fitting
#'
#' @inheritParams normalise_trial_data
#' @param num_doses Number of dose levels in the design.
#' @return A character vector of problems, empty when the data are valid.
validate_trial_data <- function(data, num_doses, day_of_assessment, obswin) {
  problems <- character()
  if (nrow(data) == 0) return("Enter at least one patient.")

  row_msg <- function(rows, what) {
    sprintf("Patient(s) %s: %s", paste(rows, collapse = ", "), what)
  }
  bad <- which(is.na(data$dose) | data$dose < 1 | data$dose > num_doses |
                 data$dose != round(data$dose))
  if (length(bad)) {
    problems <- c(problems, row_msg(bad, sprintf(
      "dose level must be a whole number from 1 to %d.", num_doses)))
  }
  bad <- which(is.na(data$entry_day) | data$entry_day < 1)
  if (length(bad)) {
    problems <- c(problems, row_msg(bad, "entry day must be 1 or later."))
  }
  bad <- which(!is.na(data$entry_day) & data$entry_day > day_of_assessment)
  if (length(bad)) {
    problems <- c(problems, row_msg(bad, sprintf(
      "entry day is after the day of assessment (day %d).",
      day_of_assessment)))
  }
  bad <- which(is.na(data$status) | !data$status %in% trial_statuses)
  if (length(bad)) {
    problems <- c(problems, row_msg(bad, sprintf(
      "status must be one of %s.", paste(trial_statuses, collapse = ", "))))
  }
  needs_days <- data$status %in% c("DLT", "Withdrawn")
  days <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(data$days_followed))
  bad <- which(needs_days & (is.na(days) | days < 1 | days > obswin))
  if (length(bad)) {
    problems <- c(problems, row_msg(bad, sprintf(
      "days followed must be from 1 to %d for DLT and Withdrawn patients.",
      obswin)))
  }
  bad <- which(needs_days & !is.na(days) & !is.na(data$entry_day) &
                 data$entry_day + days - 1 > day_of_assessment)
  if (length(bad)) {
    problems <- c(problems, row_msg(bad, sprintf(
      "follow-up runs past the day of assessment (day %d).",
      day_of_assessment)))
  }
  bad <- which(data$status %in% "Completed" & !is.na(data$entry_day) &
                 data$entry_day + obswin - 1 > day_of_assessment)
  if (length(bad)) {
    problems <- c(problems, row_msg(bad, sprintf(
      "cannot have completed the %d-day window by the day of assessment (day %d).",
      obswin, day_of_assessment)))
  }
  evaluable <- if (is.null(data$evaluable)) rep(TRUE, nrow(data)) else
    parse_evaluable(data$evaluable)
  bad <- which(is.na(evaluable))
  if (length(bad)) {
    problems <- c(problems, row_msg(bad, "evaluable must be Yes or No."))
  }
  if (!any(evaluable %in% TRUE)) {
    problems <- c(problems, "At least one patient must be evaluable.")
  }
  problems
}

#' Map the legacy app's five-column CSV to the status-based format
#'
#' The legacy upload was headerless: dose level, DLT (0/1), entry day,
#' follow-up days, still monitored for DLT (0/1).
#'
#' @param legacy A data.frame with the five legacy columns, in order.
#' @inheritParams normalise_trial_data
#' @return A data.frame with `dose`, `entry_day`, `status`, `days_followed`,
#'   `evaluable` (all evaluable).
from_legacy_format <- function(legacy, obswin) {
  stopifnot(ncol(legacy) == 5)
  names(legacy) <- c("level", "tox", "entry", "followup", "monitored")
  status <- ifelse(
    legacy$tox == 1, "DLT",
    ifelse(legacy$monitored == 1, "Ongoing",
           ifelse(legacy$followup >= obswin, "Completed", "Withdrawn"))
  )
  data.frame(
    dose = legacy$level,
    entry_day = legacy$entry,
    status = status,
    days_followed = ifelse(status %in% c("DLT", "Withdrawn"),
                           legacy$followup, NA_real_),
    evaluable = rep(TRUE, nrow(legacy))
  )
}

# Accepted spellings for each column of an uploaded file.
column_aliases <- list(
  dose = c("dose", "dose_level", "level"),
  entry_day = c("entry_day", "entry", "entry_date"),
  status = c("status", "follow_up_status", "dlt_status"),
  days_followed = c("days_followed", "followup", "follow_up", "days"),
  evaluable = c("evaluable", "dlt_evaluable", "evaluability")
)

#' Read uploaded trial data
#'
#' Accepts the status-based format (a CSV or Excel file with a header row;
#' `days_followed` and `evaluable` are optional) and the legacy headerless
#' five-column CSV.
#'
#' @param path Path to the uploaded file.
#' @param name Original file name, used to pick the reader.
#' @inheritParams normalise_trial_data
#' @return A data.frame with `dose`, `entry_day`, `status`, `days_followed`,
#'   `evaluable` (`NA` where not recognised).
read_trial_file <- function(path, name = path, obswin) {
  if (grepl("[.]xlsx?$", name, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
    raw <- as.data.frame(readxl::read_excel(path))
  } else {
    if (all(!nzchar(trimws(readLines(path, warn = FALSE))))) {
      stop("The file is empty.", call. = FALSE)
    }
    raw <- utils::read.csv(path, header = FALSE, strip.white = TRUE,
                           stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    first_row_numeric <- !anyNA(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(unlist(raw[1, ]))))
    if (ncol(raw) == 5 && first_row_numeric) {
      return(from_legacy_format(raw, obswin))
    }
    raw <- utils::read.csv(path, strip.white = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }

  key <- gsub("[^a-z]+", "_", tolower(trimws(names(raw))))
  out <- lapply(column_aliases, function(aliases) {
    hit <- match(aliases, key)
    hit <- hit[!is.na(hit)]
    if (length(hit)) raw[[hit[1]]] else NULL
  })
  missing <- setdiff(c("dose", "entry_day", "status"),
                     names(Filter(Negate(is.null), out)))
  if (length(missing)) {
    stop("Missing column(s): ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "),
         ". Expected dose, entry_day, status, days_followed.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (is.null(out$days_followed)) {
    out$days_followed <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(raw))
  }
  if (is.null(out$evaluable)) {
    out$evaluable <- rep(TRUE, nrow(raw))
  }

  # Match status case-insensitively to the canonical labels.
  status <- trimws(as.character(out$status))
  canonical <- trial_statuses[match(tolower(status), tolower(trial_statuses))]
  data.frame(
    dose = as.numeric(out$dose),
    entry_day = as.numeric(out$entry_day),
    status = ifelse(is.na(canonical), status, canonical),
    days_followed = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(out$days_followed)),
    evaluable = parse_evaluable(out$evaluable)
  )
}

#' Example trial data, also offered as the upload template
#'
#' Cohorts of three for the default design (30-day window, assessment on
#' day 50), each patient at the dose the design recommended on their entry
#' day: three patients complete dose 1; at dose 2 one completes, one is
#' withdrawn on day 24 and one has a DLT on day 33, so the third cohort
#' stays at dose 2. On day 50 the design stays at dose 2, escalating to
#' dose 3 from day 63 if no new DLTs are observed.
example_trial_data <- function() {
  data.frame(
    dose = c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2),
    entry_day = c(1, 2, 7, 9, 12, 14, 36, 37, 42),
    status = c("Completed", "Completed", "Completed", "Completed",
               "Withdrawn", "DLT", "Ongoing", "Ongoing", "Ongoing"),
    days_followed = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, 13, 20, NA, NA, NA),
    evaluable = TRUE
  )
}

name: R/messages.R
content:
# Recommendation text and model-recommendation table from a dtp_pathway.
#
# Legacy built both from fixed slots (current, T_E or T_S, complete
# follow-up): it labelled the current dose from the complete-follow-up fit
# minus one, and compared recommendations with `!=`, which errors as soon
# as any of them is NA (stopped). Here both read the pathway's runs, so any
# shape and any stopped fit is handled the same way.

describe_dose <- function(dose, current_dose) {
  if (is.na(dose)) {
    "stop the trial"
  } else if (dose > current_dose) {
    sprintf("escalate to dose level %d", dose)
  } else if (dose < current_dose) {
    sprintf("de-escalate to dose level %d", dose)
  } else {
    sprintf("stay at dose level %d", dose)
  }
}

#' Describe the recommendation and how it changes over time
#'
#' @param pathway A `dtp_pathway`.
#' @return A list with `decision` (at the day of assessment: `"D"`, `"S"`,
#'   `"E"` or `"Stop"`), `headline` (one sentence) and `details` (zero or
#'   more sentences, one per later change, then a closing note).
recommendation_text <- function(pathway) {
  runs <- pathway$runs
  t_a <- pathway$day_of_assessment
  current <- pathway$current_dose
  now <- runs$decision[1]

  if (now == "Stop") {
    return(list(
      decision = now,
      headline = sprintf(
        "Day %d: stop the trial, the lowest dose is too toxic.", t_a
      ),
      details = character()
    ))
  }

  headline <- sprintf("Day %d: %s (%s).", t_a,
                      describe_dose(runs$dose[1], current),
                      if (now == "S") "the current dose" else
                        sprintf("current dose level %d", current))
  later <- runs[-1, , drop = FALSE]
  details <- sprintf("From day %d: %s, if no new DLTs are observed by then.",
                     later$from_day,
                     vapply(later$dose, describe_dose, character(1),
                            current_dose = current))

  last_day <- max(pathway$days$day)
  closing <- if (pathway$complete_day == t_a) {
    "No patients are still in DLT follow-up."
  } else if (last_day < pathway$complete_day) {
    sprintf("Projected to day %d; follow-up completes on day %d.",
            last_day, pathway$complete_day)
  } else if (nrow(later) == 0) {
    sprintf(paste("With no new DLTs, this holds until follow-up completes",
                  "on day %d."), pathway$complete_day)
  } else {
    character()
  }

  list(decision = now, headline = headline, details = c(details, closing))
}

#' Fits at the key days of the pathway
#'
#' The day of assessment, each later change of recommendation and complete
#' follow-up. A later change falling on the complete-follow-up day is
#' reported as complete follow-up; complete follow-up on the day of
#' assessment is reported once, as current.
#'
#' @param pathway A `dtp_pathway`.
#' @return A list of `list(curve, day, fit)`, in time order.
key_fits <- function(pathway) {
  runs <- pathway$runs
  t_a <- pathway$day_of_assessment
  complete <- pathway$complete_day

  later <- seq_len(nrow(runs))[-1]
  later <- later[runs$from_day[later] != complete]
  c(
    list(list(curve = sprintf("Current (day %d)", t_a), day = t_a,
              fit = pathway$fits$current)),
    lapply(later, function(i) {
      list(curve = sprintf("From day %d", runs$from_day[i]),
           day = runs$from_day[i], fit = pathway$fits$changes[[i]])
    }),
    if (complete != t_a) {
      list(list(curve = sprintf("Complete follow-up (day %d)", complete),
                day = complete, fit = pathway$fits$complete))
    }
  )
}

#' Model recommendation at the key days of the pathway
#'
#' One row per [key_fits()] entry.
#'
#' @param pathway A `dtp_pathway`.
#' @param level Coverage of the posterior credible interval.
#' @return A data frame with `curve`, `day`, `dose` (`NA` when stopped),
#'   `decision`, and the posterior DLT probability at `dose`: `prob_tox`,
#'   `lower`, `upper` (all `NA` when stopped). `level` is kept as an
#'   attribute.
model_table <- function(pathway, level = 0.9) {
  stopifnot(is.numeric(level), length(level) == 1, level > 0, level < 1)
  tail_p <- (1 - level) / 2
  out <- do.call(rbind, lapply(key_fits(pathway), function(r) {
    dose <- escalation::recommended_dose(r$fit)
    dose <- if (is.na(dose)) NA_integer_ else as.integer(dose)
    at <- function(x) if (is.na(dose)) NA_real_ else x[dose]
    data.frame(
      curve = r$curve, day = r$day, dose = dose,
      decision = if (is.na(dose)) "Stop" else
        c("D", "S", "E")[sign(dose - pathway$current_dose) + 2],
      prob_tox = at(escalation::mean_prob_tox(r$fit)),
      lower = at(escalation::prob_tox_quantile(r$fit, tail_p)),
      upper = at(escalation::prob_tox_quantile(r$fit, 1 - tail_p))
    )
  }))
  attr(out, "level") <- level
  out
}

#' Format a model table for display
#'
#' @param table A `model_table()` result.
#' @param digits Decimal places for probabilities.
#' @return A character data frame with columns `Curve`, `Recommended dose`
#'   and `Posterior DLT rate [<level> CrI]`; stopped rows read "Stop" and
#'   have no posterior.
format_model_table <- function(table, digits = 3) {
  num <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits)
  post <- ifelse(is.na(table$dose), "—",
                 sprintf("%s [%s, %s]", num(table$prob_tox),
                         num(table$lower), num(table$upper)))
  out <- data.frame(
    table$curve,
    ifelse(is.na(table$dose), "Stop", as.character(table$dose)),
    post
  )
  names(out) <- c("Curve", "Recommended dose",
                  sprintf("Posterior DLT rate [%g%% CrI]",
                          100 * attr(table, "level")))
  out
}

name: R/palette.R
content:
# Colours shared by the bslib theme and the plots.
#
# Neutral theme with the ICR logo: navy accent, the logo's grey for
# secondary text, Okabe-Ito colours for decisions (distinguishable with
# colour-vision deficiency; legacy used a red/orange/green traffic light).

dtp_colours <- list(
  ink = "#212529",
  muted = "#616466",
  rule = "#CED4DA",
  accent = "#1F4E79",
  dlt = "#D55E00",
  # Marks for patients not in the model: 3:1 on white, enough for
  # graphics; their labels use `muted`, which reads as text.
  excluded = "#868E96",
  decision = c(D = "#0072B2", S = "#E69F00", E = "#009E73",
               Stop = "#D55E00")
)

decision_labels <- c(D = "De-escalate", S = "Stay", E = "Escalate",
                     Stop = "Stop")

#' Sequential colours for dose levels, light to dark
#'
#' Purples keep dose levels apart from the decision colours; the lightest
#' has 4.5:1 contrast on white, so it reads as text (the "D1" labels).
#'
#' @param num_doses Number of dose levels.
#' @return A character vector of `num_doses` colours.
dose_colours <- function(num_doses) {
  grDevices::colorRampPalette(c("#7D68C4", "#2E1A66"))(num_doses)
}

#' WCAG contrast ratio between two colours
#'
#' @param a,b Colours.
#' @return The ratio, from 1 to 21.
contrast_ratio <- function(a, b) {
  luminance <- function(colour) {
    rgb <- grDevices::col2rgb(colour)[, 1] / 255
    rgb <- ifelse(rgb <= 0.03928, rgb / 12.92, ((rgb + 0.055) / 1.055)^2.4)
    sum(c(0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722) * rgb)
  }
  l <- sort(c(luminance(a), luminance(b)), decreasing = TRUE)
  (l[1] + 0.05) / (l[2] + 0.05)
}

#' Black or white, whichever contrasts more with each fill
#'
#' @param fill Colours.
#' @return `"#000000"` or `"#FFFFFF"` for each.
text_on <- function(fill) {
  vapply(fill, function(f) {
    if (contrast_ratio(f, "#FFFFFF") >= contrast_ratio(f, "#000000")) {
      "#FFFFFF"
    } else {
      "#000000"
    }
  }, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
}

name: R/plots.R
content:
# Interactive plots (ggplot2 + ggiraph). # # Ports of the legacy base-graphics plots. The study timeline and the DTP # plot were the same swimmer plot, so they are one function here: without # a pathway it is the study timeline; with one, a "Next patient" row shows # the recommendation day by day. Titles belong to the cards around the # plots, so the plots carry none. theme_dtp <- function(base_size = 12) { ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) + ggplot2::theme( text = ggplot2::element_text(colour = dtp_colours$ink), axis.text = ggplot2::element_text(colour = dtp_colours$muted), panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical", legend.box.just = "left", legend.justification = "left", legend.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = ggplot2::rel(0.85)), legend.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = ggplot2::rel(0.85)) ) } status_shapes <- c(Completed = 16, Ongoing = 21, Withdrawn = 8, DLT = 4) status_colours <- c(Completed = dtp_colours$muted, Ongoing = dtp_colours$muted, Withdrawn = dtp_colours$muted, DLT = dtp_colours$dlt) #' Patient follow-up segments for the timeline #' #' Follow-up counts the entry day as day 1, so a patient followed for `d` #' days was last observed on `entry_day + d - 1`. #' #' @param data Normalised trial data, see [normalise_trial_data()]. #' @param day_of_assessment Study day of the analysis (T_A). #' @param obswin DLT observation window, in days. #' @return `data` with `last_day` (last day observed; the day of #' assessment for Ongoing patients), `window_end` (last day of the #' window; projected follow-up runs from `last_day` to it for Ongoing #' patients) and a `tooltip`. timeline_data <- function(data, day_of_assessment, obswin) { if (is.null(data$evaluable)) data$evaluable <- rep(TRUE, nrow(data)) data$last_day <- data$entry_day + data$days_followed - 1 data$window_end <- data$entry_day + obswin - 1 data$tooltip <- ifelse( data$evaluable, sprintf( "Patient %d
Dose level %d, entered day %g
%s: %g of %g days (weight %.2f)", data$patient, data$dose, data$entry_day, data$status, data$days_followed, obswin, data$weight ), sprintf( "Patient %d
Dose level %d, entered day %g
%s: %g of %g days
Not evaluable: not in the model", data$patient, data$dose, data$entry_day, data$status, data$days_followed, obswin ) ) data } #' Study timeline, with the dose transition pathway when given #' #' Non-evaluable patients are drawn in grey, without projected follow-up. #' #' @param data Normalised trial data, see [normalise_trial_data()]. #' @param day_of_assessment Study day of the analysis (T_A). #' @param obswin DLT observation window, in days. #' @param num_doses Number of dose levels (fixes the dose colours). #' @param pathway Optional `dtp_pathway` for the same data. #' @return A ggplot with ggiraph interactive layers. plot_timeline <- function(data, day_of_assessment, obswin, num_doses, pathway = NULL) { d <- timeline_data(data, day_of_assessment, obswin) # Colour by dose level, or grey when not evaluable. excluded_key <- "Not evaluable" d$dose_f <- factor(ifelse(d$evaluable, d$dose, excluded_key), levels = c(seq_len(num_doses), excluded_key)) d$status <- factor(d$status, levels = names(status_shapes)) d$label_colour <- ifelse(d$evaluable, dose_colours(num_doses)[d$dose], dtp_colours$muted) d$point_colour <- ifelse(d$evaluable, status_colours[as.character(d$status)], dtp_colours$excluded) d$id <- paste0("patient-", d$patient) n <- nrow(d) ongoing <- d[d$evaluable & d$status == "Ongoing" & d$window_end > d$last_day, , drop = FALSE] change_days <- if (!is.null(pathway)) pathway$runs$from_day[-1] day_keys <- c( sprintf("Assessment, day %d", day_of_assessment), if (length(change_days)) { sprintf("Recommendation changes, day%s %s", if (length(change_days) > 1) "s" else "", paste(change_days, collapse = ", ")) } ) present <- intersect(names(status_shapes), as.character(d$status)) p <- ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(y = patient)) + ggiraph::geom_segment_interactive( ggplot2::aes(x = entry_day, xend = last_day, yend = patient, colour = dose_f, tooltip = tooltip, data_id = id), linewidth = 1.6, lineend = "round", key_glyph = "path" ) + ggiraph::geom_segment_interactive( data = ongoing, ggplot2::aes(x = last_day, xend = window_end, yend = patient, colour = dose_f, tooltip = tooltip, data_id = id), linewidth = 1.1, linetype = "22", alpha = 0.7, show.legend = FALSE ) + ggiraph::geom_point_interactive( ggplot2::aes(x = last_day, shape = status, colour = I(point_colour), tooltip = tooltip, data_id = id), size = 2.6, stroke = 1.2, fill = "white" ) + # Labels are text, so non-evaluable ones take the darker muted grey # (4.5:1 on white) rather than the excluded grey of the marks. ggplot2::geom_text( ggplot2::aes(x = entry_day, label = paste0("D", dose), colour = I(label_colour)), hjust = 1, nudge_x = -0.6, size = 3, fontface = "bold", show.legend = FALSE ) + # Key days are named in the legend, not on the plot, where close days # would overlap. ggplot2::geom_vline( data = data.frame(x = day_of_assessment, key = day_keys[1]), ggplot2::aes(xintercept = x, linetype = key), colour = dtp_colours$ink, linewidth = 0.4, key_glyph = key_only_for("dashed", ggplot2::draw_key_path) ) + # Colours fixed by dose level; the legend lists the doses given. ggplot2::scale_colour_manual( "Dose level", values = stats::setNames(c(dose_colours(num_doses), dtp_colours$excluded), c(seq_len(num_doses), excluded_key)), breaks = c(as.character(sort(unique(d$dose[d$evaluable]))), if (!all(d$evaluable)) excluded_key), guide = ggplot2::guide_legend(order = 2) ) + ggplot2::scale_shape_manual( "DLT follow-up", values = status_shapes, breaks = present, guide = ggplot2::guide_legend( order = 3, override.aes = list(colour = unname(status_colours[present])) ) ) + ggplot2::labs(x = "Study day", y = NULL) + theme_dtp() + ggplot2::theme(panel.grid.major.y = ggplot2::element_blank()) labels <- paste0("P", d$patient) if (!is.null(pathway)) { p <- add_pathway_row(p, pathway, row = n + 1, change_key = day_keys[2]) labels <- c(labels, "Next") } p + ggplot2::scale_y_reverse(breaks = seq_along(labels), labels = labels, expand = ggplot2::expansion(add = 0.6)) + ggplot2::scale_linetype_manual( "Key days", values = c("dashed", "22")[seq_along(day_keys)], breaks = day_keys, limits = day_keys, guide = ggplot2::guide_legend(order = 4) ) + ggplot2::theme(legend.key.width = ggplot2::unit(1.6, "lines")) } add_pathway_row <- function(p, pathway, row, change_key = NULL) { # Each run covers its days up to the start of the next; the last one # holds on after it, so it is drawn a day past its last projected day. runs <- pathway$runs runs$start <- runs$from_day runs$end <- runs$to_day + 1 # "Dose 2", not "D2": on this row D reads as de-escalate. runs$label <- ifelse(runs$decision == "Stop", "Stop", ifelse(runs$end - runs$start >= 6, paste("Dose", runs$dose), runs$dose)) runs$tooltip <- sprintf( "Days %d to %d
%s%s", runs$from_day, runs$to_day, vapply(runs$dose, describe_dose, character(1), current_dose = pathway$current_dose), ifelse(runs$from_day > pathway$day_of_assessment, "
if no new DLTs are observed", "") ) runs$id <- paste0("run-", seq_len(nrow(runs))) runs$decision <- factor(runs$decision, levels = names(decision_labels)) changes <- runs[-1, , drop = FALSE] wide <- runs[runs$end - runs$start >= 2, , drop = FALSE] narrow <- runs[runs$end - runs$start < 2, , drop = FALSE] p + ggiraph::geom_rect_interactive( data = runs, ggplot2::aes(xmin = start, xmax = end, ymin = row - 0.35, ymax = row + 0.35, fill = decision, tooltip = tooltip, data_id = id), inherit.aes = FALSE ) + # Label on the bar, in black or white for contrast with its fill; # one-day runs are too narrow, so their label sits just above. ggplot2::geom_text( data = wide, ggplot2::aes(x = (start + end) / 2, y = row, label = label), inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 3, fontface = "bold", colour = text_on(dtp_colours$decision[as.character(wide$decision)]) ) + ggplot2::geom_text( data = narrow, ggplot2::aes(x = (start + end) / 2, y = row - 0.5, label = label), inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 2.6, fontface = "bold", colour = dtp_colours$ink ) + ggplot2::geom_vline( data = transform(changes, key = rep(change_key, nrow(changes))), ggplot2::aes(xintercept = start, linetype = key), colour = dtp_colours$decision[as.character(changes$decision)], linewidth = 0.5, key_glyph = key_only_for("22", ggplot2::draw_key_path, colour = dtp_colours$muted) ) + ggplot2::scale_fill_manual( "Next patient", values = dtp_colours$decision, labels = decision_labels, drop = TRUE, guide = ggplot2::guide_legend(order = 1) ) } #' Prior DLT probability quantiles of the empiric working model #' #' Under the empiric model `p_d = skeleton_d ^ exp(beta)` with #' `beta ~ N(0, variance)`, the quantile used by escalation for the #' posterior, applied to the prior. #' #' @param skeleton Prior DLT probabilities (the design's skeleton). #' @param variance Prior variance of `beta`. #' @param p Probability. prior_prob_tox_quantile <- function(skeleton, variance, p) { skeleton^exp(stats::qnorm(1 - p, mean = 0, sd = sqrt(variance))) } #' Prior and posterior dose-toxicity curves at the key days #' #' One panel per [key_fits()] entry, each with the prior for reference. #' #' @param pathway A `dtp_pathway`. #' @param skeleton Prior DLT probabilities (the design's skeleton). #' @param variance Prior variance of the model parameter (the design's). #' @param target Target DLT rate. #' @param level Coverage of the credible intervals. #' @return A data frame with `panel` (factor of panel headers, in time #' order), `curve`, `role` (`prior`, `current`, `change`, `complete`), #' `dose`, `prob_tox` (the skeleton for the prior), `lower`, `upper`, #' `recommended` (the design's recommendation, after its rules), #' `mtd_estimate` (posterior mean closest to target) and `tooltip`. #' Prior rows repeat in every panel. dose_toxicity_data <- function(pathway, skeleton, variance, target, level = 0.9) { # As model_table(). stopifnot(is.numeric(level), length(level) == 1, level > 0, level < 1) tail_p <- (1 - level) / 2 doses <- seq_along(skeleton) fits <- key_fits(pathway) roles <- c("current", rep("change", length(fits) - 1)) if (pathway$complete_day != pathway$day_of_assessment) { roles[length(roles)] <- "complete" } prior_lower <- prior_prob_tox_quantile(skeleton, variance, tail_p) prior_upper <- prior_prob_tox_quantile(skeleton, variance, 1 - tail_p) ci <- function(lower, upper) { sprintf("%g%% CrI [%.3f, %.3f]", 100 * level, lower, upper) } out <- do.call(rbind, Map(function(k, role) { rec <- escalation::recommended_dose(k$fit) mean <- escalation::mean_prob_tox(k$fit) panel <- sprintf("%s\n%s", k$curve, if (is.na(rec)) "Stop: lowest dose too toxic" else sprintf("Recommended dose %d", rec)) posterior <- data.frame( panel = panel, curve = k$curve, role = role, dose = doses, prob_tox = mean, lower = escalation::prob_tox_quantile(k$fit, tail_p), upper = escalation::prob_tox_quantile(k$fit, 1 - tail_p), recommended = !is.na(rec) & doses == rec, mtd_estimate = doses == which.min(abs(mean - target)) ) note <- ifelse( posterior$recommended, "

prior_fill, colour = NA, key_glyph = key_only_for("22", ggplot2::draw_key_rect) ) + ggplot2::geom_ribbon( data = post, ggplot2::aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper, group = panel, fill = I(colour), linetype = keys[2]), alpha = post_alpha, colour = NA, key_glyph = key_only_for("solid", ggplot2::draw_key_rect, fill = dtp_colours$ink, alpha = post_alpha) ) + ggplot2::geom_hline( data =
